concept.name: In-sample period
concept.definition: The historical interval used directly to design, fit, select, or calibrate a strategy or model.
concept.intuition: It turns an informal trading idea into a claim or design choice that can be evaluated against dated evidence.
concept.mechanics: Record the interval and every decision influenced by it; treat performance from it as development evidence rather than an independent test.
concept.failure_modes: Results can mislead when hindsight, multiple testing, nonstationarity, costs, or unavailable historical information are ignored.
concept.misconceptions: A favorable historical result is evidence about the tested sample and assumptions, not proof of a durable profitable edge.
concept.example: Parameters chosen using 2015-2020 make that entire interval in-sample even if only part was used for fitting.
